items.stem: A formula =B2*C$1 is filled down a column. Why is the C1 reference written as C$1?

options.text: To keep the row fixed on row 1 while the column fills down
options.rationale: Correct: the dollar sign before the row number locks that row so every filled formula still multiplies by C1.
The dollar sign is a reference anchor, not formatting.
It does not change the data type of C1.
Reference anchoring is unrelated to charting.

items.stem: Numbers imported into a column are left-aligned and will not sum. The most likely cause is:

options.text: They are stored as text, not numbers
options.rationale: Correct: text-stored numbers left-align and are excluded from numeric sums until converted.
Charts do not affect whether values sum.
Read-only status would block edits, not cause a failed sum.
Sheet count does not affect summation.
